claims.claim_ar: افتتاح الآية باستفهام تعجبي «وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ» ثم الانتقال إلى بيان موضوعي موجه للمخاطبين يدلّ على تحوّل في لحن الخطاب (تعجّب ثم إخبار) — تحول شخصي/خطابي (انتقال في نوع المخاطبة).
claims.claim_en: The verse opens with a rhetorical interrogative of astonishment ('And how can you disbelieve...') then shifts to an informative address to the addressees, marking a change in tone/address (a rhetorical shift between exclamation/questioning and informative statement).
claims.needs_review_reason: Distinguishing between general stylistic 'asloob' (asloob_hakim) and classical 'iltifat' can be subtle here; the quoted support is from tafsir discussion of audiences/readings rather than the verse text itself.

claims.claim_ar: وجود «وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ» عملُهُ كقَلْبٍ أو حاشية مفاجئة تُدَوِي الحضور النبوي بينهم، فيُقوّي الاستنكاف من الكفر أمام وجود الرسول والآيات بينهم (إدخال عنصر تقريبي مفاجئ لتعزيز الحجة).
claims.claim_en: The phrase 'and in you is His Messenger' functions as a sudden parenthetical insertion that emphasizes the Prophet's presence among them, strengthening the argument against disbelief by stressing the nearness of revelation and the Messenger.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classification as 'fasl_wasl' (parenthetical insertion/connection-separation) is interpretive; the source quote is from tafsir referencing the Prophet rather than the exact ayah wording in the chunk list.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تضمر مقابلة بين حالة الكفر والبعد عن الهداية وبين حالة الاعتصام بالله والهدى: مفارقة/تضاد يضع الكفر مقابل الهداية ككلٍّ متقابلٍ (تضاد بلاغي واضح).
claims.claim_en: The verse sets up a clear rhetorical contrast between disbelief (being distant from guidance) and holding fast to God (being guided): an antithesis that juxtaposes unbelief and guidance.
claims.needs_review_reason: High confidence in identifying contrast/antithesis; source quote is a Quranic parallel cited in the commentary that exemplifies this rhetorical opposition.

claims.claim_ar: استعمال «مَنْ» الشرطية/الجامعة («وَمَنْ يَعْتَصِمْ بِاللَّهِ…») لصياغة حكم عام أو قاعدة عامة: تعميمٌ يُختم بخبرٍ حاسم («فَقَدْ هُدِيَ…») — أسلوب إنشائي تُستدل به الآيات على العموم والتأكيد.
claims.claim_en: The use of the general conditional 'man' ('and whoever holds fast to God...') formulates a general rule: a universalizing conditional concluded with a decisive predicate ('then he has been guided...'), an instructive construction that creates generalization and assurance.
claims.needs_review_reason: Labeling this as 'ijab_inshaa' (a technical term for the constructive use of conditional/generalizing particles) is reasonable but terminology may vary across rhetoricians; source is a tafsir example showing similar 'ومن ي...' constructions.
